findings.finding: The adapter attempts to reject a mode-9 fatal using fingerprint.get("fingerprint_probe_fatal"), but the pinned refusal_fingerprint result never supplies that field. Its intended-classification test only checks LINK.LINK.ERR.findall(log), whose pinned regex recognizes located `...: error:` diagnostics and does not match a generic `Fatal error:`/native-exception line. Thus a mode-9 log containing the exact refusal marker and a fatal line, with exit 2 and complete snapshots, can still be classified INTENDED_DIAGNOSTIC_REFUSAL_NO_PROOF_RULE and pass _capture_errors because the fatal field is absent. This can incorrectly mark the source/MIR capture complete after a failed diagnostic verifier stage.
findings.fix: Inspect the actual strict-UTF8 mode-9 log in the adapter and reject fatal/native exception lines and any unexpected verifier errors explicitly; do not rely on the nonexistent fingerprint_probe_fatal field. Add an isolated synthetic test with the valid marker/exit/snapshots plus a fatal line and require incomplete.

nits: Although mode-9 source unchanged is indirectly required by the pinned capture classification, the adapter does not itself assert stage.source_unchanged or rehash/ghost-strip the final source pair after that stage. An explicit check would make the physical source-pair invariant direct.
